en: Regarding the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* Dharma of the Ten Rākṣasīs:
first, one desires to perform the seal of entry into the Śākyamuni Samādhi Seal.
This is the Seal of the Single Maṇḍala: with the two hands, the *dāna* and *prajñā* fingers are interlaced within; then, the two *tarjanī* (water) fingers are each [placed].
Using the two emptinesses to suppress the two fire-claws,
the remaining *pāramitās* support one another at their heads, thus completing the twenty-eight sections.
This explains the twenty-eighth chapter.
Second, the Lotus Seal: Interlace the two water fingers and the two fire fingers within;
press the tip of the earth finger with the effort finger, and press the wisdom finger with the wind finger.
To apply dhyāna to prajñā, one forms the mudrā called the "Vajra" (or *viṅga*) seal, reciting the mantra:
*Sarvadharmapudgalānām anurmanu-sarākṣa*. With both hands, each holding the water-hook (*pāśa*) with the fire-fingers (*tarjanī*) turned inward.
Furthermore, with the *ākāśa-khanya* (space-digging) *kavaca* (armor),
one suppresses the left *prajñā* (wisdom) with the right *vāyu* (wind);
one then suppresses the left *bala* (power) with the right *tejas* (fire).
Again, place the right thumb over the left; the vow is immediately accomplished. The mantra is:
*Tadyathā* | *mili mili* | *mūlu mūlu* | *huḥ svāhā*. With the previous mudrā, place the left [thumb] on top; it is immediately accomplished. The mantra is: [as above].
Tadyathā: mili mili muhu svāhā. Fifth, with the previously mentioned mudrās, each having its own distinct characteristic:
turn the thumbs and wisdom-fingers (tarjanīs) back-to-back and face them toward one another;
furthermore, hook the right wind-finger (anāmikā) with the left strength-finger (madhyamā).
The mantra is then recited: Oṃ! Eighty thousand vajra-kumāras!
Kanaka-na-hu-su-hu-su-pa-pa-pa! [Direct it] toward the direction of the ghosts; the thunder and lightning are bound by the seal. Six rākṣasas are bound by the aforementioned seal.
Then, cross the two thumbs;
press the two earth fingers (the index fingers) between the two water fingers (the middle fingers);
and further, hook the tips of the two wind fingers (the ring fingers) by bending them.
Press the thumbs against the tips [of the fingers].
The mantra says:

*Iṭi li* and so forth. As stated in the Sūtra, this is the Rākṣasa-mantra for conforming to principle. Seventh, the Seal of the Sūtra-piṭaka: Interlace the two outer fire-fingers (the index fingers) of both hands.
Place the two water [fingers] above as hooks;
again, join the two space [fingers] at their tips;
and interlace the two earth [fingers] within.
The mantra says:
"Eight rākṣasas protect the Dharma-padmagarbha seal: the two hands each cross behind the fire [fingers], with the two water-hooks."
The winds and fingers interlace;
furthermore, two earths and two voids respectively form a continuous cycle through their principles.
The mantra says:
Oṃ bhrūṃ vaṃ jyotaha. This is the seal of the nine rākṣasa-dust tāla of the original lotus. With both hands, place two fire-hooks on the backs of the water [mudrās].
Then, the left and right hands grasp one another.
Again, hold the right earth element and press it against the left force element at the face.
Again, press the right wind element upon the left wisdom element.
Form the seal by pressing the left wisdom hand upon the right dhyāna hand.
The mantra is:
Oṃ jūpaṭa jñāna svāhā. (10) This is the Great Binding Seal of the Earth, Heavens, and Māras: the left hand is turned downward and the right hand is turned upward.
Immediately, hook the right earth element with each left wisdom element;
then, hook the right water element with each left vow element;
and finally, connect them all with the space element as a lock.
Join the backs together with the right fire-hooking the left side;
furthermore, join each with the wind-sign.
The mantra says:
Oṃ cāmuṇḍe cāmuṇḍe ṭakki ṭakki vajre vajre hūṃ hūṃ. The form of the rākṣasī is like that of a yakṣa;
her garment is blue in color.
With his right hand holding a single-pronged vajra against his right shoulder and his left hand holding a rosary,
he should immediately stand upon it with his left knee.
The color of the flesh on his face is like that of a *vilamba* fruit;
his form is like that of a dragon king or a full moon,
as he faces the great ocean.
In his right hand he holds wind and clouds;
in his left hand he holds a rosary.
His robe is emerald green.
Her complexion is white as she stands before a mirror-stand; her teeth are curved, and her form is like that of a celestial maiden or immortal.
Her robes are blue and her face is bowed low;
she kneels upright before him, holding incense and flowers.
She sits in the half-lotus posture. Her teeth are like flowers.
Her form is like that of a nun.
Her robe is purple in color.
Her right hand holds a flower;
her left hand holds a flower dish, slightly lowered.
Her teeth are black, and her form is like that of a divine maiden.
The color of his robes is entirely wondrous.
His right hand holds a trident and his left hand holds a *kamaṇḍalu*.
He sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*) in the form of a guardian. He has abundant hair.
Her form is like that of a youth, with the flesh-colored complexion of the full moon.
The Gandharva woman holds a copper ring in her right hand;
her left hand is extended as if in a dance, and she kneels upright.
The form of Anantā is like that of the *Śīrṣa-sūtra*.
She constantly guards her robes, which are of a pale yellowish-green color. She holds a necklace;
her form is like that of the goddess Śrī.
The hands on both sides hold necklaces (*muktā-hāra*).
The color of the robes is gold.
The complexion is the color of flesh. He sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka-bandha*). O White Emperor!
Its form is like that of the *Dīṅmíng* (Top-Resounding) star;
it has the appearance of a woman, its robe is red and blue,
and its right hand grasps the hem of her garment.
In her left hand she holds a single-pronged [vajra] in the shape of a striking implement;
she stands with one knee bent. She robs all sentient beings of their clothing and vital essence.
Her form is like that of a daughter of Brahmā or Śakra.
Wearing armor and clad in mail,
he emerges from the crown of the head as Hayagrīva,
in a wrathful form.
The right hand holds a vajra and the left hand holds a trident;
the color of the robes is variegated;
he sits in the full lotus posture.
The mantra of the eight rākṣasas is:

Oṃ tiri tiri ṭi ṭi he he bi hūṃ vaṃ hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mantra for binding the seals and protecting the body of the ten rākṣasas and the eight nāga kings. May Nanda, Upananda, and all their classes of followers protect me! May they grant their empowerment! Ga ga ga!
The Chapter on the Introduction; the Chapter on Expedient Means and Parables; the Chapter on Resolute Belief; the Chapter on Medicinal Herbs; the Chapter on the Prediction;
the Chapter on the City of Illusion; the Chapter on the Five Hundred Disciples; the Chapter on the Prediction for Learners and Those Beyond Learning; the Chapter on the Dharma Master;
the Chapter on the Stupa of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna; the Chapter on Devadatta; the Chapter on Encouraging the Retention [of the Sutra]; and the Chapter on the Exultation of Peace and Bliss.
Chapter on the Differentiation of the Tathāgata’s Life Span; Chapter on Rejoicing in the Merits of the Dharma Master;
Chapter on the Supernatural Power of Never-Disparaging and the Entrustment; Chapter on the Bodhisattvas Medicine King and Wonderful Sound;
Chapter on the Universal Gate Dhāraṇī and King Adorned; Chapter on the Exhortation of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
The above is the mantra.
The root-heart mantra of the ten rākṣasīs is as follows:
Oṃ tadyathā oṃ icchi-mi (1) icchimidhi-mi (2) rumi rumi (3) siddha-ha siddha-ha (4) sarva-duḥkha-paha. Furthermore, there is another mantra: [as follows].

1. Oṃ varada vartmani huṃ phaṭ svāhā. 2. Oṃ hara hara riṣe svāhā. 3. Oṃ nandā-kīlini svāhā. 4. Oṃ timale timale svāhā. 5. Oṃ prani pranini dhare svāhā. 6. Oṃ kūṭadharaṇi dharaṇi svāhā. 7. Oṃ sari sari karate karate svāhā. 8. Oṃ nide nide khite khite dharaṇi svāhā. 9. Oṃ bhaṭṭe bhaṭṭe candra svāhā. 10. Oṃ śrī-prakāśavirate svāhā.
